title: Design tokens using custom properties
learningObjectives: Explain design tokens using custom properties and organise styles for maintainability.

understand.concept: Design tokens are named values for shared design decisions such as colour, spacing, type scale, border radius, and shadows. CSS custom properties can expose these tokens at :root or component scopes and be consumed with var().
understand.whyItMatters: Centralised tokens make a theme easier to update and help maintain consistency. Scope component-specific tokens where appropriate and document the intended role of each token.
understand.analogy: A design token is a named setting on a control panel that multiple components can reuse.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS cascade, inheritance, and conditional rules follow the formal cascade and at-rule processing model.

explain.narrative: The card reads its colour, spacing, and radius from shared custom properties.

practise.guidedTask: Create tokens for brand colour, surface colour, spacing, and radius. Use them in two different components and change one token to observe the shared effect.
practise.independentTask: Refactor a small stylesheet using a consistent naming or organisation strategy. Verify the computed results and document the intended rule boundaries.
